questions.answer: The repository save return is rebound and passed with the previous customer to postProcess before the saved customer is returned. The postprocessor invokes customer publication, analytics publication, audit save and consent publication in that local order. Its void @Async method and the three @Async publishers join declared EnableAsync/executor configuration, with runtime interception and executor selection unverified. The analytics send returns a thenRun callback future, which the postprocessor ignores; audit save maps and returns a repository save result, also ignored. Customer and consent use external sendSafely without inspecting its result. Synchronous exceptions stop subsequent local statements; independently dispatched failures have no source completion order. The selected methods/classes declare no shared transaction or local recovery. Broker acknowledgement, durability and SDK retry/swallowing behaviour are unobserved, so local logs and invocation order give no delivery guarantee.
